extracted.intended_audience: Congress, federal agencies, agency counsel, administrative law practitioners, and regulated parties
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and binding procedural requirements for federal agency rulemaking, adjudication, hearings, records, judicial review, and related administrative processes under the Administrative Procedure Act and accompanying Attorney General commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Agency
rubrics_metrics.description: "Agency" means each authority (whether or not within or subject to review by another agency) of the Government of the United States other than Congress, the courts, or the governments of the possessions, Territories, or the District of Columbia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Nothing in the Act shall be construed to repeal delegations of authority as provided by law. Certain entities and functions (e.g., agencies composed of representatives of the parties, courts-martial, military authority in time of war, functions expiring with hostilities, and specified statutes) are excluded from the Act's operation except as to section 5.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Person and Party
rubrics_metrics.description: "Person" includes individuals, partnerships, corporations, associations, or public or private organizations of any character other than agencies. "Party" includes any person or agency named or admitted as a party, or properly seeking and entitled as of right to be admitted as a party, in any agency proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An agency may admit any person or agency as a party for limited purposes. This definition informs who has participatory and notice rights in proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Rule and Rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: "Rule" means the whole or any part of any agency statement of general applicability designed to implement, interpret, or prescribe law or policy or to describe the organization, procedure, or practice requirements of any agency. "Rule making" means agency process for the formulation, amendment, or repeal of a rule and includes the approval or prescription for the future of rates, wages, corporate or financial structures ... prices, facilities, appliances, services, or allowances therefor, or of valuations, costs, or accounting, or practices bearing upon any of the foregoing.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rulemaking is broadly defined to include many subject matters (including prescribing future rates, wages, prices, facilities, etc.). Interpretative rules, policy statements, and organization/procedure rules are recognized categories (and in some contexts treated differently for notice/hearing). The Attorney General commentary emphasizes the significance of distinguishing rulemaking from adjudication because different procedural safeguards are appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Order and Adjudication
rubrics_metrics.description: "Order" means the whole or any part of the final disposition (whether affirmative, negative, or declaratory in form) of any agency in any matter other than rule making but including licensing. "Adjudication" means agency process for the formulation of an order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act's basic scheme classifies administrative proceedings as either rulemaking or adjudication to avoid overburdensome procedures where unnecessary and to require adequate procedural protections where individual rights are at stake.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of License and Licensing
rubrics_metrics.description: "License" includes the whole or part of any agency permit, certificate, approval, registration, charter, membership, statutory exemption, or other form of permission. "Licensing" includes agency process respecting the grant, renewal, denial, revocation, suspension, annulment, withdrawal, limitation, amendment, modification, or conditioning of a license.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensing is treated as a form of agency action often covered by adjudicatory protections and the Act's procedural rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Sanction and Relief
rubrics_metrics.description: "Sanction" includes ... (1) prohibition, requirement, limitation, or other condition affecting the freedom of any person; (2) withholding of relief; (3) imposition of any form of penalty or fine; (4) destruction, taking, seizure, or withholding of property; (5) assessment of damages, reimbursement, restitution, compensation, costs, charges, or fees; (6) requirement, revocation, or suspension of a license; or (7) taking of other compulsory or restrictive action. "Relief" includes ... (1) grant of money, assistance, license, authority, exemption, exception, privilege, or remedy; (2) recognition of any claim, right, immunity, privilege, exemption, or exception; or (3) taking of any other action beneficial to any person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Detailed enumeration clarifies what agency acts count as sanctions or relief for purposes of proceedings and judicial review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of Agency Proceeding and Agency Action
rubrics_metrics.description: "Agency proceeding" means any agency process as defined in subsections (c), (d), and (e) of this section. For the purposes of section 10, "agency action" includes the whole or part of every agency rule, order, license, sanction, relief, or the equivalent or denial thereof, or failure to act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition ties together rulemaking, adjudication, and licensing and frames what is reviewable and subject to procedural requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Information — Publication of Organizational and Procedural Descriptions
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall separately state and currently publish in the Federal Register (1) descriptions of its central and field organization; (2) the established places and methods whereby the public may secure information or make submittals or requests; (3) statements of the general course and method by which its rule making and adjudicating functions are channeled and determined, including the nature and requirements of all formal or informal procedures available as well as forms and instructions as to the scope and contents of all papers, reports, or examinations; and (4) substantive rules adopted as authorized by law and statements of general policy or interpretations formulated and adopted by the agency for the guidance of the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: No person shall be required to resort to organization or procedure not so published. Agencies must maintain current, accessible procedural information in the Federal Register.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication of Opinions and Orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall publish or, in accordance with published rule, make available to public inspection all final opinions or orders in the adjudication of cases except those required for good cause to be held confidential and not cited as precedents.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Transparency of final decisions is required unless confidentiality is justified for good cause; agencies may set published rules for availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public Records Availability
rubrics_metrics.description: Save as otherwise required by statute, matters of official record shall in accordance with published rule be made available to persons properly and directly concerned except information held confidential for good cause found.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Official records must be accessible to those directly concerned, subject to statutory or justified confidentiality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking — Notice Requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: General notice of proposed rule making shall be published in the Federal Register and shall include (1) a statement of the time, place, and nature of public rule making proceedings; (2) reference to the authority under which the rule is proposed; and (3) either the terms or substance of the proposed rule or a description of the subjects and issues involved.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: this subsection does not apply to interpretative rules, general statements of policy, rules of agency organization/procedure/practice, or where the agency for good cause finds notice and public procedure impracticable, unnecessary, or contrary to the public interest (the finding and brief reasons must be incorporated).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rulemaking — Procedural Participation and Statement of Basis
rubrics_metrics.description: After notice required by this section, the agency shall afford interested persons an opportunity to participate in the rule making through submission of written data, views, or argument with or without opportunity to present the same orally in any manner; and, after consideration of all relevant matter presented, the agency shall incorporate in any rules adopted a concise general statement of their basis and purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Where rules are required by law to be made upon the record after opportunity for or upon an agency hearing, sections 7 and 8 (adjudicatory hearing procedures) apply instead. Agencies must consider submitted material and provide a concise statement of basis and purpose in final rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule Effective Dates
rubrics_metrics.description: The required publication or service of any substantive rule (other than one granting or recognizing exemption or relieving restriction or interpretative rules and statements of policy) shall be made not less than thirty days prior to the effective date thereof except as otherwise provided by the agency upon good cause found and published with the rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Thirty-day delayed effective date is default; good-cause findings can justify shorter effective times and must be published with the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to Petition for Rulemaking
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency shall accord any interested person the right to petition for the issuance, amendment, or repeal of a rule.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must accept and consider petitions from interested persons seeking rule changes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — Notice of Hearing
rubrics_metrics.description: Persons entitled to notice of an agency hearing shall be timely informed of (1) the time, place, and nature thereof; (2) the legal authority and jurisdiction under which the hearing is to be held; and (3) the matters of fact and law asserted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When private persons are moving parties, other parties must promptly be notified of controverted factual or legal issues. Agencies may by rule require responsive pleadings. Scheduling must consider convenience and necessity of parties and representatives.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adjudication — Opportunity to Participate and Procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency shall afford all interested parties opportunity for (1) the submission and consideration of facts, argument, offers of settlement, or proposals of adjustment where time, the nature of the proceeding, and the public interest permit, and (2) to the extent that the parties are unable so to determine any controversy by consent, hearing and decision upon notice and in conformity with sections 7 and 8.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act requires opportunity to present and consider factual and legal materials, settlement proposals, and (when required) formal hearings following sections 7 and 8 procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Separation of Investigative/Adjudicative Functions
rubrics_metrics.description: Save to the extent required for the disposition of ex parte matters as authorized by law, no officer who presides at the reception of evidence shall consult any person or party on any fact in issue unless upon notice and opportunity for all parties to participate; nor shall such officer be responsible to or subject to the supervision or direction of any officer, employee, or agent engaged in the performance of investigative or prosecuting functions for any agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Personnel engaged in investigative or prosecuting functions shall not, in that or factually related cases, participate or advise in the decision or review except as witness or counsel in public proceedings. Exceptions apply for initial licenses, rate reasonableness, or where not applicable to agency members.

rubrics_metrics.name: Declaratory Orders Authorized
rubrics_metrics.description: The agency is authorized in its sound discretion, with like effect as in the case of other orders, to issue a declaratory order to terminate a controversy or remove uncertainty.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies may use declaratory orders as a procedural tool to resolve uncertainties without other adjudicatory steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appearance Rights and Representation
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person compelled to appear in person before any agency or representative thereof shall be accorded the right to be accompanied, represented, and advised by counsel, or if permitted by the agency, by other qualified representative. Every party shall be accorded the right to appear in person or by or with counsel or other duly qualified representative in any agency proceeding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Interested persons may appear before agencies for presentation, adjustment, or determination of issues. Agencies must proceed with reasonable dispatch while respecting convenience and necessity of parties. The Act does not grant or deny nonlawyers the right to represent others — that remains with agencies to allow or disallow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Investigations — Legal Authorization and Access to Transcripts
rubrics_metrics.description: No process, requirement of a report, inspection, or other investigative act or demand shall be issued, made, or enforced in any manner or for any purpose except as authorized by law. Every person compelled to submit data or evidence shall be entitled to retain or, on payment of lawfully prescribed costs, procure a copy or transcript thereof, except that in a nonpublic investigatory proceeding the witness may for good cause be limited to inspection of the official transcript of his testimony.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Investigative demands require statutory authorization. Compelled witnesses can obtain copies/transcripts subject to costs and limited protections in nonpublic proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Agency Subpoenas — Issuance and Enforcement
rubrics_metrics.description: Agency subpenas authorized by law shall be issued to any party upon request and, as may be required by rules of procedure, upon a statement or showing of general relevance and reasonable scope of the evidence sought. Upon contest the court shall sustain any such subpoena ... to the extent that it is found to be in accordance with law and, in any proceeding for enforcement, shall issue an order requiring the appearance of the witness or the production of the evidence or data under penalty of punishment for contempt in case of contumacious failure to do so.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Subpoenas should be relevant and reasonably scoped; courts enforce valid agency subpoenas and may punish contempt for noncompliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Denials — Prompt Notice and Grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: Prompt notice shall be given of the denial in whole or in part of any written application, petition, or other request of any interested person made in connection with any agency proceeding. Except in affirming a prior denial or where the denial is self-explanatory, such notice shall be accompanied by a simple statement of grounds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must promptly inform applicants of denials and provide a simple statement of reasons unless redundant or self-explanatory.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearings — Presiding Officers and Impartiality
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall preside at the taking of evidence (1) the agency, (2) one or more members of the body which comprises the agency, or (3) one or more examiners appointed as provided in this Act ... The functions of all presiding officers and of officers participating in decisions in conformity with section 8 shall be conducted in an impartial manner. Any such officer may at any time withdraw if he deems himself disqualified; and, upon the filing ... of a timely and sufficient affidavit of personal bias or disqualification ... the agency shall determine the matter as a part of the record and decision in the case.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hearing officers must be impartial; mechanisms exist for withdrawal or disqualification based on bias, with agency determination reflected in the record.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hearing Powers of Presiding Officers
rubrics_metrics.description: Officers presiding at hearings shall have authority, subject to the published rules of the agency and within its powers, to (1) administer oaths and affirmations, (2) issue subpoenas authorized by law, (3) rule upon offers of proof and receive relevant evidence, (4) take or cause depositions to be taken whenever the ends of justice would be served thereby, (5) regulate the course of the hearing, (6) hold conferences for the settlement or simplification of the issues by consent of the parties, (7) dispose of procedural requests or similar matters, (8) make decisions or recommend decisions in conformity with section 8, and (9) take any other action authorized by agency rule consistent with this Act.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Presiding officers have broad procedural and adjudicative powers limited by agency rules and the Act.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evidentiary Standards at Hearings
rubrics_metrics.description: Except as statutes otherwise provide, the proponent of a rule or order shall have the burden of proof. Any evidence, oral or documentary, may be received, but every agency shall as a matter of policy provide for the exclusion of immaterial and unduly repetitious evidence and no sanction shall be imposed or rule or order be issued except as supported by relevant, reliable, and probative evidence. Every party shall have the right to present his case or defense by oral or documentary evidence, to submit rebuttal evidence, and to conduct such cross-examination as may be required for a full and true disclosure of the facts. In rule making or determining claims for money or benefits or applications for initial licenses any agency may, where the interest of any party will not be prejudiced thereby, adopt procedures for the submission of all or part of the evidence in written form.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Proponent bears burden of proof; agencies should exclude immaterial or repetitive evidence; sanctions and orders must be supported by relevant, reliable, probative evidence; parties have rights to present, rebut, and cross-examine; written submissions may be used where appropriate without prejudice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Record for Decision
rubrics_metrics.description: The transcript of testimony and exhibits, together with all papers and requests filed in the proceeding, shall constitute the exclusive record for decision in accordance with section 8 and, upon payment of lawfully prescribed costs, shall be made available to the parties. Where any agency decision rests on official notice of a material fact not appearing in the evidence in the record, any party shall on timely request be afforded an opportunity to show the contrary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The record is exclusive for agency decisions; parties can challenge reliance on facts officially noticed but not in the record by timely showing contrary evidence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions by Subordinates and Agency Review Procedures
rubrics_metrics.description: In cases in which the agency has not presided at the reception of the evidence, the officer who presided ... shall initially decide the case or the agency shall require ... the entire record to be certified to it for initial decision. Whenever such officers make the initial decision and in the absence of either an appeal to the agency or review upon motion of the agency within time provided by rule, such decision shall without further proceedings then become the decision of the agency. On appeal from or review of the initial decisions ... the agency shall ... have all the powers which it would have in making the initial decision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial decisions by examiners or presiding officers may become final absent timely appeal; agency has broad review powers when it exercises review. Procedures for tentative decisions, certification, or omission are described for certain contexts (e.g., rulemaking, initial licenses).

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to Submit Proposed Findings and Requirements for Decisions
rubrics_metrics.description: Prior to each recommended, initial, or tentative decision, or decision upon agency review of the decision of subordinate officers the parties shall be afforded a reasonable opportunity to submit for the consideration of the officers participating in such decisions (1) proposed findings and conclusions, or (2) exceptions to the decisions or recommended decisions of subordinate officers or to tentative agency decisions, and (3) supporting reasons for such exceptions or proposed findings or conclusions. All decisions ... shall become a part of the record and include a statement of (1) findings and conclusions, as well as the basis therefor, upon all the material issues of fact, law, or discretion presented; and (2) the appropriate rule, order, sanction, relief, or denial thereof.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Parties must be allowed to present proposed findings and exceptions; agency decisions must state findings, conclusions, bases, and the specific disposition or remedy.

rubrics_metrics.name: Limits on Sanctions and Granting of Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: No sanction shall be imposed or substantive rule or order be issued except within jurisdiction delegated to the agency and as authorized by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Agencies must act within statutory jurisdiction and authority; actions beyond delegated authority are unlawful.

rubrics_metrics.name: Procedural Protections for Licenses
rubrics_metrics.description: In any case in which application is made for a license required by law the agency, with due regard to the rights or privileges of all the interested parties or adversely affected persons and with reasonable dispatch, shall set and complete any proceedings required to be conducted pursuant to sections 7 and 8 of this Act or other proceedings required by law and shall make its decision. Except in cases of willfulness or those in which public health, interest, or safety requires otherwise, no withdrawal, suspension, revocation, or annulment of any license shall be lawful unless, prior to the institution of agency proceedings therefor, facts or conduct which may warrant such action shall have been called to the attention of the licensee by the agency in writing and the licensee shall have been accorded opportunity to demonstrate or achieve compliance with all lawful requirements. In any case in which the licensee has ... made timely and sufficient application for a renewal or a new license, no license ... shall expire until such application shall have been finally determined by the agency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Licensees are entitled to procedural safeguards before adverse actions; agencies must provide notice of facts or conduct and opportunity to cure except in limited exigent circumstances; timely renewal applications prevent expiration until final determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Right to Judicial Review
rubrics_metrics.description: Any person suffering legal wrong because of any agency action, or adversely affected or aggrieved by such action within the meaning of any relevant statute, shall be entitled to judicial review thereof, except so far as (1) statutes preclude judicial review or (2) agency action is by law committed to agency discretion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial review is broadly available for legal wrongs from agency action, with statutory exceptions and deference where law commits decision to agency discretion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form, Venue, and Procedures for Judicial Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The form of proceeding for judicial review shall be any special statutory review proceeding relevant to the subject matter in any court specified by statute or, in the absence or inadequacy thereof, any applicable form of legal action (including actions for declaratory judgments or writs of prohibitory or mandatory injunction or habeas corpus) in any court of competent jurisdiction. Agency action shall be subject to judicial review in civil or criminal proceedings for judicial enforcement except to the extent that prior, adequate, and exclusive opportunity for such review is provided by law.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Judicial review can proceed via statutory review schemes or general remedies when statutory proceedings are absent or inadequate; prior exclusive remedies can limit subsequent judicial proceedings.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reviewable Acts and Finality
rubrics_metrics.description: Every agency action made reviewable by statute and every final agency action for which there is no other adequate remedy in any court shall be subject to judicial review. Any preliminary, procedural, or intermediate agency action or ruling not directly reviewable shall be subject to review upon the review of the final agency action. Except as otherwise expressly required by statute, agency action shall be final whether or not there has been presented or determined any application for a declaratory order, for any form of reconsideration, or (unless the agency otherwise requires by rule) for an appeal to superior agency authority.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Final agency actions are presumptively reviewable; interlocutory actions are reviewable as part of final action review; statutory language can alter finality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interim Relief — Agency and Court Authority
rubrics_metrics.description: Pending judicial review any agency is authorized, where it finds that justice so requires, to postpone the effective date of any action taken by it. Upon such conditions as may be required and to the extent necessary to prevent irreparable injury, every reviewing court ... is authorized to issue all necessary and appropriate process to postpone the effective date of any agency action or to preserve status or rights pending conclusion of the review proceedings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Both agencies and courts have authority to grant interim relief to preserve rights and prevent irreparable harm during review.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards (Scopes) of Judicial Review
rubrics_metrics.description: The reviewing court shall (A) compel agency action unlawfully withheld or unreasonably delayed; and (B) hold unlawful and set aside agency action, findings, and conclusions found to be (1) arbitrary, capricious, or otherwise not in accordance with law; (2) contrary to constitutional right, power, privilege, or immunity; (3) in excess of statutory jurisdiction, authority, or limitations, or short of statutory right; (4) without observance of procedure required by law; (5) unsupported by substantial evidence in any case subject to the requirements of sections 7 and 8 or other wise required on the record of an agency hearing provided by statute; or (6) unwarranted by the facts to the extent that the facts are subject to trial de novo by the reviewing court.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Courts must review questions of law and interpretation and apply the enumerated grounds (including arbitrary/capricious, procedural defects, substantial evidence, and de novo fact review where appropriate) when deciding whether to set aside agency action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Examiners — Appointment, Duties, Rotation, Removal, Compensation
rubrics_metrics.description: There shall be appointed by and for each agency as many qualified and competent examiners as may be necessary for proceedings pursuant to sections 7 and 8, who shall be assigned to cases in rotation so far as practicable and shall perform no duties inconsistent with their duties and responsibilities as examiners. Examiners shall be removable by the agency in which they are employed only for good cause established and determined by the Civil Service Commission after opportunity for hearing and upon the record thereof. Examiners shall receive compensation prescribed by the Commission independently of agency recommendations or ratings ...
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examiners are to be qualified, rotated, insulated from inconsistent duties, removable only for good cause through the Civil Service Commission, and compensated independently (though the Attorney General commentary notes practical concerns about the independence clause). Agencies temporarily understaffed may use examiners from other agencies with Commission consent. The Commission has investigatory and rulemaking powers relating to examiners.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construction and Effect — Preservation of Rights and Severability
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in this Act shall be held to diminish the constitutional rights of any person or to limit or repeal additional requirements imposed by statute or otherwise recognized by law. Except as otherwise required by law, all requirements or privileges relating to evidence or procedure shall apply equally to agencies and persons. If any provision of this Act or the application thereof is held invalid, the remainder of this Act or other applications of such provision shall not be affected. Every agency is granted all authority necessary to comply with the requirements of this Act through the issuance of rules or otherwise. No subsequent legislation shall be held to supersede or modify the provisions of this Act except to the extent that such legislation shall do so expressly. This Act shall take effect three months after its approval except that sections 7 and 8 shall take effect six months after such approval, the requirement of the selection of examiners pursuant to section 11 shall not become effective until one year after such approval, and no procedural requirement shall be mandatory as to any agency proceeding initiated prior to the effective date of such requirement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Act is to be read as preserving constitutional and other statutory rights, as severable, and provides phased-in effective dates for procedural requirements; agencies have authority to issue rules to comply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attorney General Commentary — Distinguish Rulemaking vs. Adjudication; Reasonable Construction
rubrics_metrics.description: The definitions of "rule making" and "adjudication" ... are especially significant. The basic scheme underlying this legislation is to classify all administrative proceedings into these two categories ... The statute carefully differentiates between these two basically different classes of proceedings so as to avoid, on the one hand, too cumbersonme a procedure and to require, on the other hand, an adequate procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Attorney General endorses reasonable construction of the Act that balances private and governmental interests; commentary explains why rulemaking includes prescription for future rates etc., and cautions against overly rigid or narrow drafting. This commentary serves as interpretive guidance for applying definitions and balancing procedural burdens.
